column7: 2026-11-05: Acme branch plan: sort_keys is added on main first (user does that, so upstream gets it), then brought over to this branch. On this branch only, sort_keys must default to ON (main's default is the user's call). Reason: Acme's tooling calls plain dumps() and we can't change their call sites, and their reviewers diff every config file and complain about key-order churn between drops. Root cause of the churn is how our side builds the dicts, not the writer; the writer already passes dict order through, but hoists scalars above sub-tables and switches AoTs between inline and [[...]] form at 100 chars.

2026-11-05: sort_keys landed on main in 6299ae0 (default off, as the user asked; I did not choose that). Acme branch can bring it over and flip the default to ON there only. Non-str keys with sort_keys=True raise Python's sort TypeError when mixed with str keys; I left that as is.

2026-11-05: sort_keys cherry-picked from main (6299ae0) onto acme; follow-up commit flips its default to True here only (main stays False). Legacy order-dependent tests pin sort_keys=False; README states branch default. Expect conflicts when merging/rebasing with main: keep main's default there.
